question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14122710/assets/9792a5033ccd5f6f8198e3465899c752ddd4ae0986b324c13575c1a92e1ff3c7.svg)

find $P(2\leq X \leq 6).$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that for continuous random variables, it doesn't matter whether or not we include the endpoints of the interval. So we can perform this computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 6) & =P(2<X\le 6) \\  & =P(X\le 6)-P(X\le 2) \\  & =F(6)-F(2) \\  & =\frac{{6}^{2}-25}{75}-0 \\  & =\frac{11}{75}\end{aligned}
$$
